 Advertisement UPDATES: Tornado watch issued for several counties across Oklahoma, including the OKC metro
 Advertisement Updated: 1:53 PM CST Nov 2, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Joseph Neubauer Meteorologist UPDATES: Tornado watch issued for several counties across Oklahoma, including the OKC metro
 Updated: 1:53 PM CST Nov 2, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Joseph Neubauer Meteorologist A tornado watch has been issued as severe storms move across Oklahoma on Monday afternoon and evening. 
 Two waves of storms are expected on Monday, with the second bringing the tornado risk. Severe thunderstorm warnings have already been issued for counties in central Oklahoma. 
 Advertisement KOCO 5 Meteorologist Joseph Neubauer breaks down what you need to know about the storm risk and the timeline below. 
 Live Updates 
 Oklahoma Tornado Watch 
 A tornado watch has been issued for several counties in western and central Oklahoma, including the OKC metro, until 10 p.m. Monday. Check out the image below to see where the tornado watch has been issued. 
 KOCO 5 Oklahoma Storm Risk 
 A level 3 moderate risk has been issued for the north-central part of the OKC metro to Enid, Stillwater, Tulsa, Ponca City, and Bartlesville. The rest of the OKC metro and most of Oklahoma are under a level 2 slight risk. 
 There's also a level 1 marginal risk in far western and far southeastern Oklahoma. 
 KOCO 5 
 Oklahoma Tornado Risk 
 The tornado risk also increased for areas in the level 3 enhanced risk zone. Those areas have a tornado index of 6 out of 10. 
 >> Go to the KOCO weather page | Get KOCO on the Go | Subscribe to KOCO 5's YouTube channel | Sign up for KOCO 5’s Morning Newsletter 
 Most of the slight risk zone has a tornado index of 4 out of 10, and the threat decreases in far western and southeastern Oklahoma. 
 Tornado warnings are expected to be issued with storms on Monday. 
 KOCO 5 
 Oklahoma Storm Timeline 
 While there's a chance of rain Monday morning, the severe storm risk goes up during the afternoon and evening. 
 The window for storms is 2-6 p.m. in west-central Oklahoma, 3-9 p.m. in central Oklahoma, 7-11 p.m. in east-central Oklahoma, and 10 p.m. to midnight in eastern Oklahoma. 
 KOCO 5 
 The radar predictor map shows some storms flaring up in central Oklahoma just west and north of the OKC metro around 1 p.m. Monday. Those storms aren't expected to be tornadic, but they could be severe and pack a punch with small hail and strong wind gusts. 
 KOCO 5 
 Those storms will move into north-central Oklahoma near Stillwater, Enid, Perry, and Ponca City by 2-3 p.m. That'll be part of the first wave of storms that'll move through Oklahoma. 
 KOCO 5 
 The second wave will be after 3 p.m. Monday, and those storms bring a tornado risk. Those storms in western Oklahoma are the ones that'll likely spin. 
 KOCO 5 
 There should be individual supercells in western and northern Oklahoma by 5 p.m. Those will move into central Oklahoma and the OKC metro by 6 p.m. Monday. 
 KOCO 5 
 Storms will develop into fuller supercells from 7-8 p.m. in central Oklahoma and the OKC metro. They'll be a broken line of storms with a potential for tornadoes and strong winds. 
 KOCO 5 
 That line of storms will then move past the OKC metro and into eastern Oklahoma from 9-10 p.m. Monday. 
 KOCO 5 
 Counties in eastern Oklahoma will continue to see severe storms late Monday night from 10 p.m. to midnight and into the overnight hours.
